BACKGROUND ONLY - no extraction. What it is and why no data: Country survey of e-fuel plans, resources, regulation, incentives and stakeholders. Production technologies are described qualitatively (electrolyser and methanation types, Tables 1-2) with reaction stoichiometry and enthalpies only; levelised costs appear only in reproduced IEA charts (Figs. 7-8). No capex, plant efficiency or energy per unit of product printed for an e-fuel plant. What it does have: Stoichiometry and reaction enthalpies for e-methane (-253.2 kJ/mol CH4), e-ammonia (-46.1 kJ/mol NH3) and e-methanol (pp.17-18); sensitivity statements (5-10 EUR/MWh electricity raises e-jet by about 250 EUR/t; 400 MEUR capex or 75 EUR/t CO2 equivalent); target of 60% energy conversion efficiency by 2030 (China programme); project capacities (e.g. Reintegrate Aalborg 120 MW).
